name: Chat Interceptor
description: Runs a per-room script before the agent replies; falls through to the AI when the script declines.

debug.description: Write a per-turn trace to logFile.

logFile.description: Absolute path of the debug trace file. Defaults to ~/.openclaw/logs/chat-interceptor.log

asideLogFile.description: Absolute path of the file /aside messages are appended to, one JSON object per line. Defaults to ~/.openclaw/logs/chat-interceptor-asides.log

tap.description: Enables the built-in `/tap` command: from inside a room, start an AI harness in that room's project and ask it to run its own /tap skill. Omit this block and `/tap` is left to the room's script and the AI, as before.

projectsDir.description: Directory holding one subdirectory per project. `/tap` looks for `<project>/.tap` and `<project>/genesis/.tap` under it to find the project bound to the current room; `/tap <projname>` creates `<projectsDir>/<projname>/genesis/.tap`.

projectsFile.description: Where the room-to-project table is kept, one entry per conversation. `/tap <projname>` writes it, `/tap` reads it, `/tap -uninstall` clears it. Defaults to ~/.openclaw/chat-interceptor-projects.json. It holds conversation ids, so it lives in the state directory rather than in any project.

command.description: argv of the AI harness. `prompt` is appended as the last argument and the project directory becomes its working directory. Defaults to ["claude", "-p", "--permission-mode", "bypassPermissions"]. Use an absolute executable path: the gateway runs as a service and its PATH may differ from a shell.

continueCommand.description: argv used instead of `command` once the harness has already run in this project, so it carries on the same session and remembers what it asked. E.g. ["claude", "-p", "--continue", "--permission-mode", "bypassPermissions"]. Omit to start every round fresh. Whether a project has run before is read from `projectsFile`, not guessed; a continued run that fails clears the mark so the next one starts fresh.

prompt.description: What to ask the harness to do. The default invokes the harness's own /tap skill and tells it the one thing it cannot know on its own: the run is non-interactive, so it must not stop at a question, and its closing summary is what reaches the user.

notifyCommand.description: argv used to report a finished run back to the room; `--channel <c> --target <t> --message <text>` are appended to it. Defaults to ["openclaw", "message", "send"].

env.description: Extra environment variables for the harness, merged over the gateway's own.

timeoutMs.description: Kill the harness after this long. Defaults to 1800000 (30 minutes).

autoInstall.description: After a successful harness run, install whatever `<project>/genesis/route.json` describes, unless the same route is already live. Defaults to true, so a project goes live as soon as it can run and the user can test it straight away. Set false to require an explicit `/tap -install`.

interpreters.description: How to run a script by file extension, as an argv prefix that the script path is appended to. Example: a .py entry of [C:/tools/uv.exe, run] makes the route run that script with uv. Only needed for extensions the plugin cannot resolve itself: .mjs/.js/.cjs always use the gateway own Node binary, and .py falls back to uv (then python) found on PATH at install time.

allowFrom.description: Sender ids allowed to run `/tap`. Omit to allow anyone in the room. `/tap` starts an agent that can write files on this machine, so set this for any room you do not fully control.

routes.description: Per-conversation script routes. The first route whose channel and target match wins; no match means the turn goes to the AI unchanged.

name.description: Label used in traces and error messages.

channel.description: Channel/provider id, e.g. "telegram" or "discord". Omit to match any channel.

target.description: Conversation to intercept, in `openclaw message send --target` form. Bare ids ("-1001234567890"), prefixed ids ("channel:123456789012345678"), and fully qualified ids ("discord:channel:123456789012345678") all resolve to the same room.

project.description: Name of a directory under tap.projectsDir. The script and the interpreter are worked out by convention every time the route runs: scripts/intercept.{mjs,js,cjs,py} inside that project, run with the gateway own Node for JavaScript or with uv (then python) for Python. Nothing machine-specific ends up in the config, so it keeps working across Node and uv upgrades. Give this or command.

command.description: argv of the script, as an escape hatch when the project convention does not fit. Wins over project. Use absolute executable paths: the gateway runs as a service and its PATH may differ from a shell.

env.description: Extra environment variables merged over the gateway's own.

timeoutMs.description: Kill the script after this long. Defaults to 15000.

onError.description: What to do when the script fails. "handle" (default) replies with the error; "passthrough" hands the turn to the AI. Only use passthrough for scripts with no side effects.
